findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: The bleach available for assisting in the clean up of vomit/diarrhea isn’t an EPA approved chemical. The bleach is low splash and it lacks an EPA registration number. Ensure to purchase a regular bottle of bleach. Also, be sure that it has an EPA registration number and is approved to effectively kill norovirus. Will follow-up on October 5, 2026 to see that regular bleach has been purchased.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The faucet spout at the triple sink inside of the dish room is in disrepair. When water is turned on, the spout falls from the faucet. Ensure that the faucet is repaired by a licensed plumber.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: There is a significant amount of ice build on the inner surfaces of the reach in freezer along the bar station. When time permits, be sure to unplug and defrost the freezer to melt the ice. Ensure that ice build up is maintained in freezer.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: Both hand-sinks in the kitchen and dish areas lacked hot water. The knobs at the hand-sinks appear to be broken, which is preventing hot water availability at the sinks. Ensure that all hand sinks are provided with hot water to be sure that hands are getting washed properly. Will follow-up on October 5, 2026 to see that sinks are repaired.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
At least two of the employees working at the time of inspection could not show proof of food handler certificates. Ensure that all employees who handle food or clean dishes are food handler certified if not food manager certified. Be sure that all certificates are printed out for future inspections. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were several insect glue traps that contained at least 15 dead roaches throughout the facility. There weren’t any live roaches found, however, each of the glue traps contained many dead insects. The facility contracts with Bacon’s Termite & Pest Control as their pest provider. The owner mentioned that the traps are old and have not been replaced in several months. Ensure that the premise is free of insects (live or dead) and to monitor the presence of insects through trapping devices and keeping the facility clean. Will follow-up on April 27, 2026 to check on the replacement of traps.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: There were unwrapped straws mixed with wrapped straws on top of the bar’s counter. The unwrapped straws are in close proximity to customers are presents exposure to the food contact surface. Ensure to purchase wrapped straws or place the unwrapped behind the counter where they are controlled by employees.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility was observed operating without sanitizer solutions. The restaurant had recently opened and was in the process of serving customers upon arrival. Two sanitizer buckets were prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are always present if the facility is preparing, handling, and serving food to the public.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas inside of the kitchen are in need of cleaning:
- underneath the prep table (directly next to the prep cooler)
- walls behind the prep table that’s mentioned above

The floor has accumulated food debris underneath the prep table and the wall contains dried grease. Ensure that these areas are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulated debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was an egg shell observed in the kitchen’s hand-sink. Discussed with person-in-charge (PIC) and the shell was discarded. Ensure that hand-sinks are only used for handwashing purposes and never food prep or as a dump sink.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were several sliced deli meats that lacked date marking inside of the kitchen prep cooler. Discussed proper date marking with the PIC and date marking labels were provided to the food items. Ensure that all sliced deli meats are date marked if being held in house longer than 24 hours. Be sure to discard if seven days are exceeded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: There was a spray bottle of a cleaning chemical stored on the bottom shelf of the prep table. There was also single service items and equipment used for cooking stored on the shelf. Discussed with PIC and the bottle was moved to the storage area where other hazardous chemicals are stored. Ensure that hazardous chemicals are never stored with food or items that will come in contact with food to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: There were several utensils and dishes with dried food debris in a container on a storage rack (in the kitchen area). Discussed and shown to PIC. Be sure to clean dishes at a frequency to preclude debris accumulation during storage.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: The owner’s Food Protection Manager Certification has expired. The owner is currently in the process of renewing her managers license. Ensure that there is at least 2 employees that are manager certified to cover all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.Q

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to turn off faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed proper handwashing procedures with PIC. Ensure that a barrier (paper towel) is used to operate faucet handles after washing hands to avoid recontaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Cooked tater tots were observed at room temperature and was tempted at 94F. Discussed with PIC that cooked potatoes are considered TCS (time/temperature control for safety) and will need to be hot held. PIC placed tater tots and fries under a heat lamp to correct the violation. Be sure that TCS foods are maintained at 135F or above to ensure proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer bucket available for the bar area. Discussed with the PIC and a bucket was prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat). Ensure there is a sani bucket present in both the bar and kitchen area during all hours of operation.

findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of a deep cleaning: 
- floors and walls around/behind pieces of equipment
- shelves of kitchen equipment
-outer surfaces of table top cooking equipment

Ensure that non food contact surfaces and physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup of food and grease debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

The owner is currently in the process of renewing her managers license, along with getting the main cook manager certified. Ensure that there is at least 2 employees that are manager certified to cover all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.Q@

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: A head of lettuce stored in the kitchen prep cooler was observed uncovered and touching salad dressing bottles. Discussed the possibilities of contamination and the lettuce head was discarded. Ensure that food stored in cold holding equipment contain coverings or be stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer bucket present in the kitchen area while food preparation was occurring. Discussed with PIC the need for a sani bucket. A sanitizer solution was created and tested at 100ppm (CL). Be sure that there is a sanitizer bucket present during hours of operation to ensure that food contact surfaces are properly getting sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the interior of the microwave to be soiled with dried food debris. The soiled areas were shown to the PIC. The surfaces were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure inside surfaces of the microwave are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent the accumulation of dried food debris and possible contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
The straws that are stored in the bar area are uncovered and are in close proximity to the customers. Discussed with PIC and straws were placed behind the counter and away from customers. Ensure that unwrapped straws are stored in a manner that protects against contamination. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Bleach is being used to sanitize dishes at the triple sink. Chlorine test strips were not available. However, quaternary ammonia is being used for sanitizer buckets and quat test were available. PIC mentioned that CL test strips will be purchased soon. Ensure that chlorine test strips are available to properly measure sanitizing concentrations. 

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the interior of the microwave to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC and surfaces were cleaned. Ensure inside surfaces of the microwave are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
There wasn’t a CFPM at the start of the inspection. CFPM arrived before inspection ended. Ensure that a CFPM is available at all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed PIC not wash hands before engaging in food preparation. PIC shook inspector’s hand and proceeded to prepare food. Discussed with PIC to wash hands before engaging in food production. Ensure that hands are washed before engaging in food production after switching tasks. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed PIC using bare hands to touch a ready-to-eat food item. PIC mentioned that the facility just received boxes of gloves prior to inspector’s arrival. Ensure that employees do not use  bare hand contact with RTE foods. 

3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the inside of the microwave to be soiled with food debris. Also observed the ice freezer to have an accumulation of frost and ice buildup. The freezer is used to store ice for the drinks in the bar area. Ensure that equipment of food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained as frequent as necessary to prevent contamination.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several food items not to be date marked in a prep cooler in the kitchen area. These items include but aren't limited to deli meats, cheeses, and salads. PIC discarded some food items and the others were date marked with the appropriate opening date. Ensure that TCS foods that are held in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parmesan).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of bleach to be stored on a shelf mixed with single service items. Discussed with PIC and bottle of bleach was removed. Ensure that chemicals are always stored separate from single service items in order to prevent contamination.  

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed clean utensils stored in a container with food debris at the bottom. Discussed with PIC and container was switched. Ensure that utensils are always stored in manner that prevents them from contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment:
Observed the handwashing sink in the dish machine area to not have an adequate flow of hot water. PIC mentioned that the hand-sink barely gets used. Ensure that hand-sinks always have an adequate flow of hot water to properly wash hands. 

5-103.12: Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, EQUIPMENT, and nonFOOD EQUIPMENT that are required to use water except that water (A) and (B) to a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or in response to a temporary interruption of a water supply need not be under pressure.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Overall, the facility is need of a deep cleaning. 
- floors, walls, sides and underneath of equipment are soiled with food debris and splatter. 
- Shelving in the kitchen area has food debris
- Wall behind dish machine (mold on caulk where dish machine and wall meet)
Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulated debris.  

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PIC is not allergen trained. Ensure that all CFPMs are allergen trained. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
